tier_reason: Lowered C to D: the enricher read both April 2025 web harnesses and found the two counts are not comparable. skia-benchmark (7b5a2e9, SkiaView.cpp) times Skia with flushAndSubmit(GrSyncCpu::kYes), which waits for the GPU, while tgfx-benchmark (245ed1a, TGFXBaseView.cpp) times TGFX with flushAndSubmit() and syncCpu false (and since November 2025 defers submit by one frame); the ramp and stop rule keys on that draw time, so Skia stops sooner and TGFX's rectangle count can climb past what really renders at 60 FPS. The 510,308 versus 34,721 rectangles (14.7x) is therefore inflated by an unknown amount, and no valid number remains; only Skia is linked with -sASSERTIONS=2, the wasm-mt build runs TGFX vertex generation on worker threads while Skia records on one thread, and a user test in issue #381 (TGFX 1.2.1, pre-batching) found Skia far faster. Directional at best.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No valid number: the first-party '510,308 Rectangles at 60 FPS' for TGFX versus '34,721' for Skia m136 (about 14.7x, derived) comes from harnesses whose timing differs (Skia waits for the GPU with GrSyncCpu::kYes, TGFX submits without waiting), so the TGFX count can exceed what renders at 60 FPS by an unknown factor. The announcement's 'at least 10 times faster than Skia' and 'up to 16 times' rest on that comparison.
corrections.caveats: Harness asymmetry invalidates the headline (GPU sync on the Skia side only; one-frame deferred submit on the TGFX side since November 2025; Skia alone built with -sASSERTIONS=2; TGFX vertex generation on worker threads in the wasm-mt build). First-party with no GPU model, driver, OS, browser or resolution; tgfx.org/benchmark is blocked here. A user test in issue #381 (TGFX 1.2.1) found Skia far faster before TGFX's batching work; open bug #1172 (thin polygon strips).

tier_reason: Tier C stands; the 477x hatch figure is a harness artefact and is removed from the claim: the x/image/vector run resets and draws one rasteriser per page-spanning 45-degree line, so the 2,000 lines pay for per-outline bounding boxes totalling about 3.6e9 pixels (derived), whereas one page-sized x/image/vector pass would take about 40 ms (derived, unmeasured) against stilus's 70 ms. The page-clip asymmetry (stilus clips a 10 mm margin, the others do not) skips about 9% of the short strokes, a small help to the 2.0x row; the comparison times are go test means while the Numbers table is the minimum of 15.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README comparison table, 20,000 short strokes: stilus 55 ms versus x/image/vector 111 ms (about 2.0x, derived from page data; stilus clips a 10 mm page margin that skips about 9% of the strokes) and gogpu/gg 2,090 ms. The 2,000 hatch-line row (stilus 70 ms versus x/image/vector 33,400 ms, about 477x) is a harness artefact: the x/image/vector side re-creates a page-spanning rasteriser per line (about 3.6e9 bounding-box pixels in total, derived); a single page-sized pass would take roughly 40 ms (derived, unmeasured). Separate 'Numbers' table (minimum of 15): stilus 1 core 67 ms (2,000 hatch lines at 0.35 mm) and 41 ms (20,000 short strokes), 4 cores 19 ms and 12 ms.
